summary_short: Fixed a case-sensitive header include issue in `wm-app` that broke non-Windows builds.
summary_full: I inspected the workspace first and found the active Git repository under `/home/pooria/wm/wm-app`. The highest-confidence issue was a case mismatch between the real header file name `SocketDma.h` and two source includes using `socketDma.h`. That works on case-insensitive environments but fails on Linux. I updated both includes to match the actual filename and then verified both translation units with `gcc -fsyntax-only` using the STM32 include paths.
what_changed: Updated `main.c` to include `SocketDma.h` with the correct filename casing.
Updated `SocketDma.c` to include `SocketDma.h` with the correct filename casing.
Confirmed there are no remaining `socketDma.h` references in the repository.

checks.details: `gcc -fsyntax-only` completed successfully for `Core/Src/main.c` with the STM32 include paths.

result_for_user: The repository inspection is complete and the minimal fix has been applied in `/home/pooria/wm/wm-app`. The code now uses the correct header filename casing, so this source no longer fails immediately on Linux or other case-sensitive filesystems for that reason.
next_steps: If you want, I can continue with a broader compile-safety pass on `wm-app` and fix the next build blocker.
